logic_errors.title: Finite runs never finish when all workers stall before every operation has been scheduled
logic_errors.details: Expired operations correctly remain outstanding to prevent duplicate work, but continue occupying all four scheduling slots. Operations not yet started retain attempts=0 forever, so finite_done never becomes true. One pool with read, used, snapshots, health and the default status operation is already enough to trigger this. Removed/readded operations can suffer the same starvation behind permanently outstanding old generations.
logic_errors.evidence: Isolated .venv Python probe patched CommandController.run to threading.Event().wait(), then called interactive_monitor with tank -n 1 -i 0.01 --command-timeout 0.05 -c read,used,snapshots,health. It timed out at the external 2-second limit instead of terminating. The existing never-returning-worker test covers only one operation and passes.
logic_errors.recommendation: Retain the outstanding-work cap, but give finite invocations an explicit terminal path when permanently expired workers make remaining attempts impossible; mark unschedulable operations unavailable without spawning replacements and return the appropriate nonzero/partial exit status. Add coverage for more operations than workers and removed/readded pools behind saturated workers.

logic_errors.title: Missing latency fields retain an old value while acquiring a fresh group timestamp
logic_errors.details: parse_iostat accepts a seven-field row without latency fields. _collect_sample then omits requested latency keys, and interactive_monitor merges values into the previous row without clearing the group's keys first. A new read value advances measured[key] while an old read_wait/write_wait/total_wait remains displayed as current.
logic_errors.evidence: Real interactive scheduler probe used two successful command responses: 'tank 1 9 1 1 7 8 11 12', then 'tank 1 9 1 1 99 88', with -n 2 --no-status -c read,read_wait,sample_age. Final row had read=99 and stale read_wait=11; _measured_at advanced from 966406.283551731 to 966406.38377217. Exit status was 0.
logic_errors.recommendation: Before merging each successful operation, initialize all requested keys in that operation to None, or require _collect_sample to return every requested key explicitly. Add the full-to-short iostat transition test, not only malformed-row exception tests.

logic_errors.title: Public run_command singleton initialization is not thread-safe
logic_errors.details: Concurrent first callers can both observe no controller and construct separate controllers, defeating shared duplicate-command and four-child limits. The same race applies when replacing a stopped controller.
logic_errors.evidence: A deterministic two-thread probe placed a barrier inside a CommandController subclass constructor, reset _command_controller=None, and invoked public run_command concurrently for the same command. Two controller instances were constructed and two distinct instances were used.
logic_errors.recommendation: Protect lazy initialization/replacement with a dedicated lock or initialize a single controller eagerly. Test simultaneous public API first calls and stopped-controller replacement.

logic_errors.title: Old command cleanup can remove a newer same-key child from tracking
logic_errors.details: A completed child's run invocation may still be closing its files while another caller prunes the completed child and starts a replacement under the same command key. The old finally block unconditionally pops the key, removing the replacement. The replacement is then absent from close() cancellation and outstanding/duplicate limits.
logic_errors.evidence: A deterministic mocked-Popen/TemporaryFile probe paused the first invocation in output.close(), started a second live child for the same key, and released old cleanup. children changed from length 1 to 0 while the replacement run thread was still alive.
logic_errors.recommendation: Remove the entry only if self.children.get(key) is child. Add a same-command overlap test in which the first process has exited but its caller has not finished cleanup.

suggestions.details: The release-focused suite passed: 14 tests in 2.35 seconds, run through .venv with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and pytest cache disabled. A real sleeping subprocess was timed out in 0.045 seconds and controller.close() returned in 0.0 seconds at displayed precision. Existing unreapable-child cap/nonblocking-close coverage passed. Ordinary ValueError callback exceptions are transported as results and do not kill the worker: a subsequent callback returned 42. Short and nonnumeric iostat rows raise ZfsCommandError.

Static inspection confirms generation identity is checked before applying a result, removed-pool results are ignored, and outstanding entries are retained across reconciliation, preventing replacement work for the same operation until old work completes. These are sound protections against late removed/readded results; saturation/finite termination remains the exception described in ASYNC-1.

BoundedWorkers catches Exception, not BaseException, and interactive_monitor assumes successful internal results have the expected shape. Current internal callbacks normally satisfy that contract and parser errors are contained. If arbitrary callback injection is intended as a supported extension point, document the contract or validate successful result shapes before mutating UI state.

Review was limited to CommandController, BoundedWorkers, interactive_monitor, public run_command, and their directly used parsing/freshness paths. Source was not changed. Probes ran as inline Python with bytecode disabled; pytest cache was disabled. The only intentionally written review artifact is verification/async-review.json. No unrelated security audit was performed; no shell-injection or secret finding was identified in the reviewed command path.

summary: FAIL: targeted release tests pass and bounded cancellation/exception transport largely work, but independent probes reproduce finite-count starvation, stale latency falsely marked fresh, and two concurrency races in the public command execution path.
